verdict.rationale: Adyen documents that it replaces card data with a network token when cardholders add cards to wallets like Apple Pay or Google Pay, and that it sends webhooks for network token lifecycle events. That gives developers some visibility into tokens created for a card. The evidence shows no API to list or manage tokens, no wallet or merchant attribution per token, and no token-level revocation. Card suspend/close controls act on the card itself, not on individual tokens. Missing for 10: token list/retrieve API, token management/update endpoints, documented wallet/merchant identification per token, revoking a token independently of the PAN, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, network tokens are first-class — I can see and manage the tokens created for a card, know which wallet or merchant holds them, and revoke them independently of the PAN

citations.quote: Adyen sends webhooks for events in network token lifecycles. When your cardholders add their Adyen-issued cards to digital wallets like Apple Pay or Google Pay, Adyen replaces the card data with a network token.
